qAndA.question: What direction does the z-axis in the ECI frame point?

qAndA.answer: It points towards the Vernal Equinox, a key point in the sun's apparent path as seen from Earth.
qAndA.question: What is the significance of the x-axis in the ECI frame?

qAndA.answer: To illustrate how a point on Earth rotates with time while the axes of the ECI frame remain fixed.
qAndA.question: What is the purpose of drawing the example with the point 'P' on the Earth?

qAndA.answer: The point where the sun's apparent path crosses the equatorial plane while ascending.
qAndA.question: What is the Vernal Equinox?

qAndA.answer: It provides a non-rotating reference frame, making it easier to define fixed points like the Vernal Equinox.
qAndA.question: Why is the ECI frame important for understanding the Vernal Equinox?

text_to_speech: So let’s talk about the earth centered inertial frame or the ECI frame. Now this frame has got its origin at the center of the earth and it has got three mutually perpendicular axis the x-axis, the y- axis and the z-axis. The z-axis points towards the geographical north pole, the x-axis points towards the vernal equinox and the y-axis, it completes the right hand coordinate system. So here you will notice that the z-axis coincides with the spin axis of the earth. By spin axis of the earth I mean the axis about which the earth spins. This axis passes through the north pole and south pole of the earth i.e the geographical north pole and the geographical south pole. Now, you’ll see that the earth keeps spinning about its spin axis which coincides with the z axis. However, the x, y and z they do not spin. So the ECI frame is a perfectly inertial frame. To make it more clear, let me give you an example. Suppose this is an x degree longitude. This is the position of x degree longitude at time t. let’s call the time to. At time t=to this is the position of x degree longitude. At time t=to+∆t the position of the x degree longitude won’t be here but it will be somewhere over here. Suppose this is the position 1 at time t, then this will be the position 2 at time to+∆t. So at time t=to the x degree longitude will be somewhere over here and at t=to+∆t the x degree logitude will come somewhere over here because of the earth’s spin. But the x ,y and z axis they’ll be pointing towards the same point. X will always be pointing towards the vernal equinox, z will always be pointing towards the north pole and y will be making the right hand coordinate system. So I have been mentioning this word quite frequently ‘vernal equinox’. So let’s see what this vernal equinox is. Suppose this is our earth, this will be our 0 degree latitude which is the equator. The plane containing the equator is called the equatorial plane. Now if you observe from the earth , then the sun will appear to orbit the earth somewhat like this- if this is position of the sun at time to, then at time t0+∆t this will be the new position of the sun. So it’ll keep on going like this. It’ll come down and down and down and down again and then it’ll stop descending at this point it’ll start ascending it’ll go up and up and up and up and up and over here it’ll start descending again. So now you observe that the sun pierces the equatorial plane at two points. The first one is over here and the second one, somewhere over here. This point where the sun passes through the equitorial plane while going up is called the ascending node of the sun. And this point where the sun goes down and passes through the equatorial plane is called descending node. This ascending node of the sun has got another name and that name is vernal equinox.
